title: The Fitting ideals of a finite type module represent the loci where it is generated by r sections and where it is locally free of rank r

standard_prerequisites.name: Fitting ideals of a finite type module and their behaviour over affine opens, as cited from the more-algebra chapter, including that over an affine open the n-th Fitting ideal becomes the whole ring for large n
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives part (1), the emptiness of the intersection of the closed subschemes defined by the Fitting ideals.

standard_prerequisites.name: Base change of Fitting ideals and the same-chapter criteria for a module to be locally generated by r sections, respectively to be finite locally free of rank r, in terms of the r-th and the (r-1)-st Fitting ideal
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts the functorial statements (2) and (3) into statements about the vanishing of the pullback of a Fitting ideal.

standard_prerequisites.name: For a finitely presented module the Fitting ideals are of finite type, so the closed immersions they cut out are of finite presentation, and a retrocompact open in the image of such an immersion is of finite presentation
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the final finite presentation assertions about the three morphisms.

core_obligations: Part (1): over every affine open there is an integer n with the n-th Fitting ideal equal to the structure sheaf, namely the number of generators of the module over that affine open, so the intersection of all the closed subschemes Z_r is empty (proof lines 1424-1427).

Part (2): for a morphism of test schemes, base change of Fitting ideals together with the same-chapter criterion shows that the pullback of the module is locally generated by at most r sections exactly when the pullback of the r-th Fitting ideal is the structure sheaf, which is exactly the condition that the morphism factors through the open complement of Z_r (proof lines 1429-1434).

Part (3): the same two cited criteria show that the pullback is free of rank r exactly when the pullbacks of the r-th and of the (r-1)-st Fitting ideal are the structure sheaf and zero respectively, which is the condition defining the locally closed subscheme Z_{r-1} minus Z_r (proof lines 1436-1444).

Finite presentation: if the module is of finite presentation then each Fitting ideal is of finite type, so each Z_r is of finite presentation over the base; the difference Z_{r-1} minus Z_r is a retrocompact open inside Z_r, hence also of finite presentation over the base (proof lines 1446-1456).
proof_roadmap: Prove the emptiness of the intersection by a local generator count (proof lines 1424-1427), then translate the two functors of the statement into pullback conditions on the r-th and (r-1)-st Fitting ideals (proof lines 1429-1444).
Add the finite presentation assertions by citing the finite typeness of the Fitting ideals of a finitely presented module and the retrocompactness of the open difference (proof lines 1446-1456).
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the Fitting ideals of a finite type quasi-coherent module with the loci where the module can be generated by at most r sections and where it is locally free of rank r, and adds finite presentation statements for those loci when the module is finitely presented (statement lines 1383-1422). The counted proof is short but does two things: it proves the emptiness of the intersection of the Fitting closed subschemes by a local generator count over affine opens, and it translates the two representable functors of the statement into pullback conditions on the r-th and the (r-1)-st Fitting ideal using base change and the same-chapter criteria (proof lines 1424-1456). It is H2: the work is the correct identification of the functors involved, and the cited inputs are the standard base change and criterion statements.
